periods.analysis: Life expectancy is 81.6 years in 2024-Q3, above the >=80 target and in green status. This is our starting point for the series, so there is no quarter-over-quarter movement to report yet. The rolling estimate reflects continued strength in preventable mortality reduction, with the Harborview CARES registry showing steady blood-pressure control in the East Pier and North Bluff clinic panels. We should read this as a healthy baseline, not a finish line.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the prevention-first approach by keeping the CARES hypertension nurse calls on a 30-day cadence for patients with systolic readings above 140. Extend the mobile vaccination and screening van to the Ferry Terminal route two Fridays per month before winter respiratory season. Ask Vital Records and EMS to continue monthly mortality-cause reconciliation so we can detect any early shift in overdose, falls, or cardiac deaths.

periods.analysis: Life expectancy is 81.0 years in 2024-Q4, down 0.6 years from 81.6, but still above the >=80 target and green. The decline is consistent with the winter respiratory period and a small increase in late-year deaths among residents over 75, especially in the assisted-living cluster near Marina Ridge. Harborview remains in a strong population-health position, but the movement tells us prevention has to stay close to the highest-risk households. Flu and COVID booster uptake improved on the Route 7 senior shuttle clinics, which likely helped keep the quarter from moving closer to the target line.
periods.recommendations: Maintain green performance by repeating the Route 7 senior shuttle vaccine clinics in January and adding one evening clinic at Coastline Community Clinic. Have the epidemiology team review 2024-Q4 respiratory and cardiac mortality by census tract before the February Public HealthStat meeting. Continue home-based fall-risk assessments through the Safe Steps program for residents discharged from Harborview Medical Center.

periods.analysis: Life expectancy is 81.3 years in 2025-Q1, up 0.3 years from 81.0 and still green against the >=80 target. That rebound suggests the winter prevention work held, particularly booster outreach, post-discharge calls, and medication checks by the Community Paramedicine Unit. We also saw better continuity for diabetes and hypertension patients in the Beacon Hill and Old Harbor panels after the January appointment-recall sprint. The signal is encouraging, but it is still a rolling measure and must be protected quarter by quarter.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the appointment-recall sprint by giving clinics a monthly list of patients overdue for A1c, blood-pressure, and lipid follow-up. Extend Community Paramedicine medication reconciliation to all heart-failure discharges within 72 hours, starting with Harborview Medical Center Unit 4B. Keep vaccine outreach open at libraries through March so the respiratory-season gains do not fade early.

periods.analysis: Life expectancy is 81.3 years in 2025-Q2, unchanged from 81.3 in 2025-Q1 and green. A flat quarter at this level is a good result for a fast-growing city, because new residents add demand before primary-care relationships are fully established. The Maternal and Child Health team enrolled 118 additional families in Harborview StartWell, and the chronic-disease team kept its East Pier hypertension cohort active through text reminders and Saturday checks. Stability here means the prevention system is absorbing growth without losing ground.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the East Pier hypertension cohort and add a second Saturday check site at the South Harbor YMCA. Extend StartWell enrollment through the permitting desk welcome packet for new multifamily buildings, so new families see WIC, pediatric, and immunization resources immediately. Monitor preventable emergency-department use monthly for new ZIP+4 growth areas along Bayline Avenue.

periods.analysis: Life expectancy is 81.8 years in 2025-Q3, up 0.5 years from 81.3 and solidly green. This is the strongest quarter in the series so far and aligns with lower summer cardiac transports and continued gains in controlled hypertension among residents tracked in CARES. The heat-response work also mattered: cooling-center shuttle stops at Pier Park, Civic Library, and Juniper Towers gave older adults a practical way to avoid heat stress during the July heat advisory. The result is a reminder that prevention is often operational and local, not abstract.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the heat-response model by pre-contracting cooling-center shuttle routes with Harbor Transit before next summer. Extend CARES blood-pressure outreach to the North Bluff apartments where EMS logged repeat cardiac calls in June and July. Keep pharmacy partners at Seaside Rx and Mercado Pharmacy supplying no-cost cuff checks and same-week referral cards.

periods.analysis: Life expectancy is 81.3 years in 2025-Q4, down 0.5 years from 81.8, while remaining green and above the >=80 target. The movement is not unexpected after a very strong summer quarter, but it does bring us back to the level seen in 2025-Q1 and 2025-Q2. Preliminary death-certificate review points to seasonal respiratory illness and several fall-related deaths among adults over 80, rather than a broad deterioration across the population. Our posture should be calm and active: the city is healthy, and the watch item is winter vulnerability among older adults.
periods.recommendations: Sustain green status by running a December-to-February respiratory protection plan with boosters, masks, and antiviral navigation at senior housing sites. Extend Safe Steps fall-prevention visits to Juniper Towers, Marina Ridge, and the Harbor Arms buildings, using fire crews for smoke-alarm and trip-hazard checks during the same visit. Review antiviral prescription lag time with Coastline Community Clinic and urgent-care vendors, with a goal of treatment starts within 48 hours of symptom report.

periods.analysis: Life expectancy is 81.3 years in 2026-Q1, unchanged from 81.3 in 2025-Q4 and green. Holding steady through the winter quarter is meaningful, especially after the 2025-Q4 decline from 81.8. Booster clinics, antiviral navigation, and Safe Steps visits appear to have limited further seasonal loss, though we should not overstate a single quarter. The population-health picture remains favorable, with the main task being to keep preventable deaths from clustering in known high-risk groups.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the winter package through March, not just through the holidays, with particular attention to residents over 75 living alone. Extend the EMS-public health weekly review of repeat 911 callers to include social-work referral disposition, not just call counts. Prepare a spring prevention push on walking safety and chronic-disease follow-up before summer activity and tourism increase exposure.

periods.analysis: Life expectancy is 81.6 years in 2026-Q2, up 0.3 years from 81.3 and green. This closes the arc near where we began in 2024-Q3, with Harborview still above the >=80 target after absorbing growth, winter illness, and seasonal risk. The improvement is consistent with better chronic-disease follow-up, fewer repeat EMS transports among the monitored cardiac cohort, and continued StartWell enrollment in new family households. Clinically, this is a stable and healthy pattern; operationally, it tells us the prevention infrastructure is working and should be widened carefully.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the CARES, StartWell, Safe Steps, and vaccine-navigation programs as core public-health infrastructure in the FY2027 workplan. Extend the chronic-disease dashboard to stratify life-expectancy drivers by age band, tract, race and ethnicity, and housing status so gains are shared across Harborview. Formalize quarterly mortality-review huddles with EMS, clinics, and Vital Records to keep this green result early-warning capable.

periods.analysis: The displayed 81.6 years is carried forward from June and remains above the 80-year target. There is no new September life-expectancy observation in this reporting slice, so a Q3 outcome cannot yet be assessed.
periods.recommendations: Confirm the next Vital Records update and retain mortality-review and prevention work while awaiting an updated result.
